significance.justification: Verified true, the conclusion would be that a "compact, language-agnostic concept subspace" peaks in the "middle third of layers," while early and late layers retain more language-specific information, and that this subspace is causally necessary and sufficient for cross-lingual concept transfer. This combines a form-(iii) ordering/invariance claim with a form-(ii) causal mechanism, establishing both a layerwise phenomenon and a mechanism that predicts where cross-language read/write should succeed; work such as Wendler et al., “Do Llamas Work in English?” (ACL 2024), shows why the location and form of multilingual abstraction are consequential mechanistic questions. The branches are determinate: a negative result would rule out the specific compact linear middle-layer bottleneck, although it would leave distributed or nonlinear sharing viable. In the topic-substitution check, the broad multilingual-representation topic alone would earn only the median score; the middle-third ordering and causal sufficiency provide a modest claim-specific increment rather than a general law of language distance or interference.

reach.justification: The named handle is a "controllable interface for cross-lingual concept editing": an extracted shared subspace and a concept vector that can be written in one language and read in another. Concept injection is ex ante with respect to the generated behavior and could be used by model editors, while the layerwise variance decomposition is primarily a post-hoc research diagnostic. After re-extraction on another model, the hypothesis predicts a middle-layer peak and language-invariant read/write behavior rather than merely supplying a search procedure, but the claim itself cautions that the substance "may not generalize across model scales or instruction-tuned vs base models," limiting asserted scope and uptake mainly to multilingual-model researchers and editors. The topic-substitution check does not preserve this score: multilingual representation alone supplies no reusable handle, whereas the cross-language editing interface and transferable layer ordering do.
